author: Nelev
body:
## Summary

Cleanups from a reuse / simplification / efficiency / altitude review of the Clerk auth work (#31–#34). No behaviour change.

- **`auth/session.py`**: non-session tokens are refused with the SDK's own `get_token_type(token) != TokenType.SESSION_TOKEN` — the classification `verify_token_async` dispatches on — instead of a hand-built list of `TokenPrefix` values.
- **`api/session.ts`**: a single check. Signed out, `getToken()` returns nothing, so the separate `userId` check repeated it; the one-caller `sessionToken` helper is folded into `authorization`.
- **Tests**: duplicated 401 cases and the two verified-email tests folded into parametrized tests; the two "refuses to ask" UI tests merged; a stale comment in `test_main.py` removed.
- **README**: a troubleshooting line about `404 User not found` that no longer applies is removed; test counts corrected.

## Left for later

- `proxy.ts` uses `createRouteMatcher`, which Clerk has deprecated. Removing it keeps today's routes protected (the page and Server Action check the session themselves) but gives up "new pages are protected by default" — a decision, not a cleanup.
- Smaller efficiency items (a duplicate `auth()` per page render, one user lookup per request, `CLERK_JWT_KEY` in production) were skipped as behaviour changes or not worth the churn.

## Test plan

- [x] medas-api: `ruff check`, `ruff format` on changed files, `pytest` — 109 pass
- [x] medas-ui: lint, typecheck, `format:check`, `yarn test` — 30 pass
- [x] Signed out, `/` still redirects to `/sign-in`
